evidence: Plaut. Am. 250: ibi nostrīs animus additust
Cic. Fam. 5.2.8: virtūte atque animō resistere (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The mind and heart in general (see mind), and so the courage in them; in verse often plural, animī. Bonō animō es is “cheer up”, “don’t be afraid”.
Daring, good or bad: as often recklessness as courage.

phrases.latin: nunc animīs opus, Aenēā, nunc pectore firmō.
phrases.english: now you need courage, Aeneas, now a steady heart.

phrases.latin: Perduellēs penetrant sē in fugam; ibi nostrīs animus additust.
phrases.english: The enemy take to their heels; at that our men got their nerve.

phrases.latin: crēvit ex metū aliēnō, ut fit, audācia
phrases.english: as usually happens, their boldness grew out of the other side’s fear

sources: Lewis & Short: animus · Lewis & Short: audacia
